_readme: Where a person can actually sell Pokemon cards, and what each venue costs.
THE SOURCING RULE, and it is the whole file. A fee number is in here ONLY if
it was read on that company's own fee, help or seller page, in a browser, and
the exact url it came from is recorded against it in `sources`. Not a blog,
not a comparison site, not a forum, not a search snippet. Where a number could
not be sourced that way it is simply ABSENT and the venue carries a link to
its own fee page instead, so a reader can go and look. A venue with no
percentage is fine. An invented percentage is not.
This is the same discipline grading.json runs on, for the same reason: on the
last recheck of that file three of its four published figures turned out to be
wrong, and every one of them had been believable.
FEE STRUCTURES ARE CONDITIONAL AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART. Flattening a
venue to one percentage is how this page would lie. Four things that a single
number always hides:
1. THE HEADLINE RATE IS OFTEN NOT THE ONLY RATE. TCGplayer's 10.75% is a
commission; on top of it sits a transaction fee of 2.5% + $0.30. Whatnot's
8% has a 2.9% + $0.30 payment processing fee on top. eBay is the odd one
out and says so on its own page: one final value fee, no separate
processing fee, but a per-order fee of $0.30 or $0.40 sits inside it.
2. WHAT THE PERCENTAGE IS TAKEN ON DIFFERS, AND THE TWO HALVES OF ONE FEE CAN
DIFFER FROM EACH OTHER. TCGplayer's commission is on the order SUBTOTAL
while its transaction fee is on the order TOTAL including shipping and
tax. Whatnot's commission excludes shipping and tax while its processing
fee includes both. eBay's final value fee is on the whole sale including
buyer-paid shipping and sales tax. So identical sale prices produce
different takes depending on what the buyer paid to ship.
3. THE RATE MOVES WITH YOUR ACCOUNT, NOT JUST THE ITEM. eBay charges 13.25%
in Collectible Card Games with no Store, and 12.35% with a Basic Store or
above, which is a paid subscription. TCGplayer charges 10.75%, 9.25% or
8.95% depending on seller type.
4. FLOORS, CAPS AND FIXED FEES. TCGplayer caps commission at $75 per product.
eBay Live caps commission at $100 per item. Fanatics Collect takes a
minimum $3 commission per Weekly Auction sale. Goldin charges $5 on a lot
that sells under $50 or draws no bid at all. Every one of those is
recorded where it was published.
A BUYLIST HAS NO FEES AT ALL AND THAT IS NOT THE BARGAIN IT SOUNDS LIKE. Troll
and Toad, Card Cavern, Dave and Adam's and a local shop all buy the card
outright, so there is no commission, no processing fee and no payout wait. The
cost is the buy price: they pay below market because they have to resell at
market. That spread is usually wider than any marketplace commission, and it is
the real number to compare. Where a buylist publishes its actual buy prices
they are recorded, because those ARE the fee.
ONE VENUE'S RATE DEPENDS ON YOUR MONTH RATHER THAN YOUR CARD. Sportlots sets
commission from your TOTAL MONTHLY SALES, from 75% at the bottom to 15% at the
top, then discounts the expensive part of each sale before it counts. Nothing
else here works that way and averaging it into a single number destroys it.
UNVERIFIED MEANS UNVERIFIED. Heritage Auctions is in here with no seller
commission because none of its own pages that could be reached publish one, and
its terms page refused the browser twice. That gap is the honest answer and it
is not filled in from somewhere else.
NO ADVICE AND NO RANKING. This file records what each venue is and what it
costs. It does not say which one to use, because that depends on the card, on
how fast the money is wanted, and on whether shipping a package is worth the
trouble. The page lets a reader choose.
THE IN-PERSON OPTION IS A REAL VENUE, NOT A FOOTNOTE. Selling to a local shop
or across a table at a card show has no commission, no payment processing fee,
no shipping, and no payout wait. The trade is the price: a shop buys at a
percentage of market because it has to resell the card at market. No Rochester
shop publishes that percentage, so no percentage is recorded here. See
shops.json and shows.json, which already carry the local ones.
IF `checked` IS MORE THAN A COUPLE OF MONTHS OLD, treat these as the SHAPE of
each venue's pricing rather than a quote, and click through. Several of these
pages carry their own last-updated stamp and were updated within days of this
check.
Percentages are US rates in USD. `sources` on every venue lists the exact urls
read and the date they were read.
GROUP is which section of the page a venue sits in, and it is stated here
rather than worked out from the prose. The builder used to guess by pattern
matching `type` and `format`, and it put eBay, Whatnot and Sportlots under
'Consignment and auction. They sell it for you' because all three mention an
auction format. Sportlots' own note in this file says in as many words that
nobody sells your cards for you there. A one word field cannot drift like
that.
market   you list it, a buyer finds it, you ship it
buylist  they buy it outright at their price
consign  you hand the cards over and they sell them for you
person   cash, face to face

venues.name: eBay
venues.format: Fixed price and auction, plus eBay Live for livestream selling
venues.bestFor: Anything with a price history: graded slabs, single high-value cards, sealed product. The per-order fee and the flat percentage make cheap singles hard to move at a profit.
venues.access: An eBay account. A Store is an optional paid subscription and it lowers the rate.

fees.what: Final value fee, Toys & Hobbies > Collectible Card Games, no Store or Starter Store
fees.rate: 13.25% up to $7,500 per item, then 2.35% on the portion over $7,500
fees.appliesTo: Total amount of the sale: item price, handling, buyer-paid shipping, sales tax and any other applicable fees
fees.note: Non-Sport Trading Cards, Sports Trading Cards and Comic Books & Memorabilia carry the same 13.25%. Most other categories are 13.6%.

fees.what: Final value fee, same category, Basic / Premium / Anchor / Enterprise Store
fees.rate: 12.35% up to $2,500 per item, then 2.35% on the portion over $2,500
fees.appliesTo: Same total amount of the sale
fees.note: A subscription buys 0.9 points off the rate but moves the band edge down from $7,500 to $2,500, so on a big single card the Store is not automatically cheaper.

fees.rate: $0.30 on orders of $10.00 or less, $0.40 on orders over $10.00
fees.appliesTo: Each order, where an order is any number of items bought by the same buyer at checkout with the same shipping method
fees.note: Charged on top of the percentage, inside the same final value fee.
eBay's own wording: one final value fee, and 'you don't have to worry about third-party payment processing fees'. This is the main structural difference from TCGplayer and Whatnot.

fees.rate: First 250 listings free each month, then $0.35 per listing with no Store
fees.appliesTo: Per listing and per category, non-refundable if the item does not sell
fees.note: Store allocations are larger and cheaper: Starter 250 then $0.30; Basic 250 auction in select categories and 1,000 fixed price all categories, then $0.25; Premium 500 / 10,000 then $0.15 and $0.10; Anchor 1,000 / 25,000 then $0.10 and $0.05. Good 'Til Cancelled listings renew monthly and are charged again each renewal.

fees.rate: Starter $7.95 a month, or $4.95 a month on yearly renewal. Basic $27.95 / $21.95. Premium $74.95 / $59.95. Anchor $349.95 / $299.95. Enterprise $2,999.95, yearly only.
fees.appliesTo: Monthly, until cancelled
fees.note: Starter Store pays the same 13.25% as no Store at all. The lower 12.35% starts at Basic.

fees.appliesTo: Each dispute where the seller is found responsible for the disputed amount, for example a chargeback
fees.note: Waived when the transaction is eligible under payment dispute seller protections.

fees.rate: 1.65% of the total amount of the sale
fees.appliesTo: Sales where the delivery address or the buyer's registered address is outside the US
fees.note: Not charged if the item ships through eBay International Shipping.

fees.rate: $5.00 or 7.5% of the reserve price, whichever is greater, capped at $250
fees.appliesTo: Auction listings with a reserve
fees.note: Charged whether or not the item sells.

fees.what: Additional final value fee for seller performance
fees.rate: +6% of the applicable final value fees, rising to +7% after four or more consecutive months
fees.appliesTo: Accounts evaluated Below Standard on the 20th of the month, applied to the following calendar month
fees.note: Separately, a 'Very High' rate of item-not-as-described return requests adds +5%, rising to +6% after four consecutive months. Only one of the two is charged if both apply.

fees.rate: 6% commission on the total amount of the sale, capped at $100 per item, plus 2.9% payment processing plus $0.30 per order
fees.appliesTo: Purchases made during an eBay Live event, and all case break purchases whenever made
fees.note: eBay states this as 8.9% + $0.30, and the 6% cap is reached at $1,667, above which only the 2.9% continues. No insertion fee on Live listings. A promotion through 31 December 2026 drops the per-order fee to $0.10 on orders of $10 or less. Different structure and much lower rate than the same seller's ordinary eBay listings.

venues.payout: Sales proceeds show as Processing, then typically become Available 1 to 2 days after the buyer's payment is confirmed. Payouts default to daily and are initiated about 2 days after payment is confirmed; weekly go out Tuesdays, biweekly every second Tuesday, monthly on the first Tuesday. The bank then typically takes another 1 to 3 business days. Express payout to a verified debit card or eligible bank account arrives in about 30 minutes for a flat $2.00. Must be a checking account or a Visa/Mastercard debit card; a savings account or PayPal cannot receive payouts.
venues.protection: Seller protections cover abusive buyer behavior (negative and neutral feedback and defects removed, cases removed from service metrics) and events outside the seller's control such as carrier delays or severe weather when tracking shows on-time shipment. Payment dispute protection, where the transaction is eligible, covers the disputed amount, waives the $20 dispute fee and removes related feedback. The extra Top Rated Seller protections against a false 'not as described' claim, and against an item returned used or damaged, require Top Rated Seller status, US or Canada residence, no 'Very High' service metric, a listing on eBay.com and a 30-day or longer return policy. Protection is lost for false identity, not honoring your own return policy, taking sales off eBay, shipping slower than the service bought, and abuse of the protections themselves.

sources.what: Category rates, per-order fee, insertion fees, dispute fee, international fee, reserve fee, performance surcharges
Store subscription prices, Store insertion allocations, Store category rates including Collectible Card Games at 12.35%
eBay Live commission, cap, processing fee and per-order promotion
Payout schedules, timing and the $2.00 express payout fee
What seller protections cover and the eligibility conditions

venues.note: eBay's own seller center page (ebay.com/sellercenter) timed out repeatedly; every figure here came from the help center articles listed above, which are eBay's own fee pages.

venues.name: TCGplayer
venues.format: Fixed price singles, with a catalogue keyed to card and condition
venues.bestFor: Raw singles at every price point, including the cheap ones, because buyers arrive searching for a named card rather than browsing.
venues.access: A seller account. New sellers start at Level 1 and the level caps how much you can list, not what you pay.

fees.appliesTo: Order subtotal
fees.note: Capped at $75 per product sold. This is the rate an ordinary individual seller pays.

fees.appliesTo: Order TOTAL: items + shipping + tax
fees.note: This is the part the headline rate hides. The commission is taken on the subtotal, the transaction fee on the total including what the buyer paid to ship, so buyer-paid shipping is charged even though it is not revenue. International orders are 3.5% + $0.30.

fees.what: Marketplace commission, Pro (non-Direct) or Sync account
fees.appliesTo: Order subtotal, capped at $75 per product
fees.note: Pro accounts additionally pay a Pro fee of 2.5% of subtotal, also capped at $75 per product. Sync accounts (Crystal Commerce, BinderPOS, Ion Sync) pay a Sync fee set entirely by the sync provider instead.

fees.appliesTo: Order subtotal, capped at $75 per item
fees.note: 8.95% is the number people quote for TCGplayer and it is the hardest one to actually pay: it comes with the Direct Fee below and is not the ordinary individual seller's rate.

fees.rate: Cards under $2.49: 50% of card value. Cards over $2.49: $1.12 per card plus all standard fees.
fees.appliesTo: Direct orders only, per item
fees.note: For cards under $2.49 the commission, Pro, Sync and transaction fees are omitted and the 50% is the whole charge.

fees.appliesTo: Non-US sellers paid through PayPal
fees.note: Taken as an account adjustment rather than deducted from the order.

venues.payout: Payments are initiated every Monday and Thursday for sales sitting at 'Completed - Pending Payment', with fees already deducted. A sale reaches that status 24 hours after confirmed delivery, or 24 hours after the expected delivery date if tracking cannot be confirmed or the order shipped without tracking. Direct deposit usually lands about four business days later. Orders shipped outside the US are payable 21 days after the order is marked shipped.
venues.protection: TCGplayer's own fee and payment pages state one thing plainly and it cuts against the seller: if an order is under review because of a buyer dispute, the funds are held until the outcome is decided, and if the order was already paid out an equivalent amount is held back from future deposits. No broader seller protection scheme was found on the pages read.

sellerLevels.limits: Up to 100 items listed at once, $1,000 total value, $500 maximum on any one item, 100 items entered per day
sellerLevels.toAdvance: 2 orders that have reached their expected delivery date, and 80% or better feedback

sellerLevels.limits: Up to 500 items, $5,000 total, $1,000 maximum per item, 500 entered per day
sellerLevels.toAdvance: 11 orders reaching EDD, and 85% or better feedback

sellerLevels.limits: Up to 50,000 items, $100,000 total, $20,000 maximum per item, no daily entry limit
sellerLevels.toAdvance: 51 orders reaching EDD, and 90% or better feedback

sellerLevels.limits: Unlimited listings, plus custom shipping options and pricing import/export

sources.what: The full fee table by seller type, the $75 per-product cap, the Direct Fee tiers, what each fee is taken on. Its own change log shows edits on 17 June 2026.
Same commission rates restated as a table, and the note that card-paid commission is taken on item + shipping + tax
Level 1 to 4 listing limits and the requirements to move up
Monday and Thursday payment runs, the 24-hour rule, the 21-day international rule, dispute holds

venues.note: TCGplayer's fee page returns 403 to automated fetching. Every figure here was read in a browser on help.tcgplayer.com.

venues.name: Whatnot
venues.format: Livestream shows with in-stream auctions and Buy It Now, plus a marketplace
venues.bestFor: Selling in volume in real time: rips, breaks, lots and singles that benefit from being shown on camera.
venues.access: A seller application is required. You must be at least 13, and 13 to 17 needs a parent or guardian's permission and a special application. Most applicants get access within minutes; some categories are gated and need a second approval.

fees.rate: 8% on the final sale price up to $1,500, and 0% on the portion above $1,500
fees.appliesTo: The item's final sale price, EXCLUDING shipping and taxes
fees.note: Whatnot's own page flags the 0%-above-$1,500 band as limited time. The 8% also covers Comics, Sports Singles and Toys & Hobbies. Coins & Money is 4%.

fees.appliesTo: Total order value: the item's final sale price plus any buyer-paid shipping plus buyer-paid taxes
fees.note: This is why '8%' is not 8%. Two identical sale prices produce different take-home because the processing fee moves with shipping and tax. Fees are calculated per transaction even when several purchases are later bundled into one shipment, so each per-transaction $0.30 is charged separately.

fees.appliesTo: The seller fees themselves
fees.note: Applied automatically and reflected in earnings.
Whatnot charges nothing to create, store or manage listings. Giveaways carry no seller fees at all because the buyer pays nothing; the seller still pays shipping.

fees.what: Free or reduced shipping you absorb
fees.appliesTo: Whatever share of shipping the seller covers
fees.note: Covering shipping also slightly lowers the processing fee, because the buyer pays less and the total order value falls.

venues.payout: For most US sellers earnings become available up to 4 hours after the carrier confirms delivery, then a requested payout reaches the bank in 1 to 2 business days. Sellers eligible for Early Payout get earnings the moment a shipping label is generated instead of waiting for delivery. Shipping methods without standard tracking run on fixed clocks instead: USPS First-Class Mail Letter (plain white envelope) is 10 days after label generation, bring-your-own-label is 7 days after the tracking number is entered.
venues.protection: Whatnot covers, and does not charge back to the seller: carrier delays after a timely drop-off, packages lost, undelivered or misdelivered by the carrier, and claims it judges to be abusive or fraudulent buyer behavior. It handles chargebacks and payment disputes itself rather than passing them to the seller. The seller is charged back for late or unverified shipment (orders must ship within two business days with valid drop-off evidence such as an in-app scanner photo or a carrier acceptance scan; from 2 March 2026 sellers are responsible for refunds on late US domestic shipments without that confirmation), for failing to fulfill a high-value item, and for refunds arising from policy violations. Coverage is not unlimited: repeated issues cause Whatnot to reassess eligibility and recover refunded amounts across orders.

sources.what: Commission by category and region, the $1,500 band, processing fee, what each is taken on. Page stamped updated 11 August 2026.
When earnings become available by country, Early Payout, and the fixed clocks for untracked methods. Page stamped 12 August 2026.
That an application is required, age rules, gated categories. Page stamped 10 August 2026.
What Whatnot absorbs and what it recovers from the seller. Page stamped 17 June 2026.

venues.note: help.whatnot.com returns 403 to automated fetching. Every figure here was read in a browser.

venues.name: COMC
venues.format: You mail cards in, COMC images, catalogues, stores and ships them; you set prices and never touch the card again
venues.bestFor: Bulk. Hundreds of mid and low value cards you do not want to list, photograph or ship one at a time. Standard and Select cap the list price at $100 a card, so high-value slabs belong on Elite or elsewhere.
venues.access: An account, and enough store credit on it to cover the processing fees when the batch is processed, or the items go on hold.

fees.rate: $2.00 per raw card, $2.50 per graded, $5.00 oversized
fees.appliesTo: Per item, charged upfront before the card can be listed
fees.note: 2 week guaranteed turnaround, no minimum fee, high resolution photos, and the only service that allows eBay auction transfer and Take Offers.

fees.rate: $1.00 per raw card, $1.50 per graded, $4.00 oversized
fees.appliesTo: Per item, upfront
fees.note: 4 week turnaround, $3.00 minimum fee per submission, $100 maximum list price per card.

fees.rate: $0.65 per raw card, $1.25 per graded, $3.50 oversized
fees.appliesTo: Per item, upfront
fees.note: 16 week turnaround and a $65.00 MINIMUM FEE, which is the real gate: below roughly 100 raw cards you are paying the minimum whatever you send. $100 maximum list price per card.

fees.appliesTo: Toploaders, card savers and one-touches on Standard and Select submissions
fees.note: No fee for penny sleeves or team bags at any level, and no toploader fee on Elite.

fees.appliesTo: Standard and Select cards valued above $100 that COMC upgrades at its discretion
Fixed-price sales, whether they sell on COMC or through COMC on eBay
fees.note: Charged when the card sells, on top of the processing fee already paid.

fees.appliesTo: Turning COMC store credit into money
fees.note: The single biggest thing a COMC quote leaves out. Proceeds arrive as store credit; taking them as cash costs 10%, may be higher for international users, and a mailed check carries an additional check fee.

fees.appliesTo: Items with an asking price over $0.75, billed on the first of the month
fees.note: First 90 days exempt for the card's original owner. Cards priced at 75 cents or less, and cards not for sale, are stored free.

fees.rate: 1 cent per $1,000 of total list price per day
fees.appliesTo: Items with a list price of $50.01 or more
fees.note: No grace period at all, unlike storage. Items at $50.00 or less are unaffected.

fees.rate: Store credit payout 4% with a $0.99 minimum. eBay Live 5% with a $2.00 minimum. Cash payout: 92% of sale price minus $5.00 under $1,000, or 95% over $1,000.
fees.appliesTo: Cards moved from COMC inventory into a COMC-run eBay auction
fees.note: Direct-to-cash auctions for in-hand cards use the same variable payout scale.

venues.payout: Sale proceeds land as COMC store credit, immediately usable to buy other cards on COMC. Converting to money costs the 10% cash-out fee, plus a check fee if you want a check rather than PayPal. Processing fees are charged out of store credit when the batch is ready to be added to inventory, so the account has to be funded before the cards arrive.
venues.protection: Not established from the pages read. COMC holds and ships the cards itself, so the seller is not exposed to buyer shipping disputes in the way a self-shipping marketplace seller is, but no seller protection policy was located on the fee pages read.

sources.what: Consignment rates by service level, turnarounds, minimum fees, holder removal, eBay auction fees and variable payouts. Resolves to COMC's own support article at comc.zendesk.com, stamped updated 4 days before this check.
Same article at its canonical url
The 5% transaction fee and the 10% cash-out fee
Storage fee, its exemptions, and the enhanced security fee

venues.note: comc.com returns 403 to automated fetching. Every figure here was read in a browser.

venues.name: Mercari
venues.format: Fixed price listings, general resale rather than card-specific
venues.bestFor: Singles, lots and sealed product aimed at a general audience rather than a card catalogue. No card database, so listings are written by hand.
venues.access: An account. No subscription, no application, free to list.

fees.appliesTo: The combined amount of the item price and buyer-paid shipping
fees.note: Effective 6 January 2025. The flattest structure of any venue here: one percentage, no per-order fee, no tier.
The old buyer-side processing fee of $0.50 + 2.9% was removed on 6 January 2025 for new and updated listings.

fees.appliesTo: Optional fast withdrawal to an eligible debit card
fees.note: Limited to $600 a month and once a day.

fees.appliesTo: Standard bank withdrawal

fees.what: Buyer Protection fee, paid by the buyer
fees.appliesTo: the item price and buyer-paid shipping
fees.note: Introduced on the same day the old buyer fee was removed, January 6 2025. It is not taken from the seller, but it is what the buyer actually spends, and this file records the buyer-paid premium at every other venue for exactly that reason.

venues.payout: Buyers have 72 hours from delivery to rate the order, after which the funds release to the seller's balance. Standard direct deposit is free; Instant Pay to a debit card costs $3.
venues.protection: Mercari states up to $200 of Shipping Protection against loss or damage in transit when the item ships on a Mercari prepaid label. It holds and releases funds itself rather than passing payment between buyer and seller, and runs fraud monitoring on transactions. The seller has 3 days to pack and drop off; shipping independently means tracking must be supplied before payment is released.

sources.what: The 10% selling fee, what it applies to, the removal of the processing fee, Instant Pay and direct deposit fees
The $200 shipping protection cap, the 3-day drop-off window, the 72-hour rating window

venues.note: Mercari's dedicated 'When do I get paid?' article (help_center/article/91) returned no readable body, so the payout timing here is what articles 169 and the seller-protection topic page state rather than that article. The flattest SELLER structure of any venue here, which is not the same as the cheapest for the person buying: see the 3.6% buyer fee above.

venues.name: Fanatics Collect (formerly PWCC)
venues.type: Consignment vault, auction house and fixed-price marketplace
venues.format: Weekly Auction, monthly Premier Auction, and an always-on Buy Now marketplace, all fed from a vault you ship cards into
venues.bestFor: Graded slabs and authenticated sealed product. Raw cards have to go through one of its grading partners first.
venues.access: An account and a vault. Items must be graded or authenticated by an accepted company (PSA, SGC, BGS, BVG, BCCG, CGC Cards, CSG, MBA and others by category) or sent raw through its authentication partners. Buying in the Premier Auction needs an application; selling does not.

fees.what: Weekly and Premier Auction seller fee
fees.rate: None on graded collectibles. The seller receives 100% of the hammer price plus a bonus commission.
fees.appliesTo: Auction sales
fees.note: A minimum $3 commission is taken from each Weekly Auction sale, which is the floor that makes the '0%' honest on cheap lots.

fees.what: Auction bonus commission, by hammer price
fees.appliesTo: Paid on top of 100% of hammer, so total commission runs 100% to 115% of hammer
fees.note: Read off Fanatics Collect's own Commission Overview chart published on its How It Works page.

fees.appliesTo: Both Weekly and Premier Auctions
fees.note: Paid by the buyer, not the seller, but it is what the bidder is really spending and therefore what suppresses the hammer. There is no buyer's premium in Buy Now.

fees.rate: 6% if the listing is priced under 120% of Card Ladder market value, 12% if priced at or above it
fees.appliesTo: The final sale price, not the original list price
fees.note: No minimum fee. If a listing is priced above the threshold but an offer is accepted that lands below it, the 6% applies.

fees.appliesTo: Eligible US sellers who choose to be paid in FanCash instead of cash, on both Buy Now and Auction sales
fees.note: Must be selected at listing; accounts default to cash with the standard fee. Vault fees tied to the sale are still charged. No cap on FanCash earned.

fees.appliesTo: Collectibles valued under $50 curated into the vault and neither submitted to auction nor sold within 30 days
fees.note: Also charged if an unsold collectible is sitting in the vault, not listed in an auction, on the 1st of a month.

fees.appliesTo: Wax and memorabilia
fees.note: Fanatics Collect says only that 'there are small additional fees for special items like wax and memorabilia'. No figure is published, so none is recorded.

venues.payout: Buy Now purchases are paid by the buyer immediately at checkout. Proceeds land as an account balance, which you either spend on Fanatics Collect or withdraw. Withdrawals are requested on the web dashboard only, and payouts are issued every Wednesday against a midnight-ET Tuesday deadline; miss it and you wait a week. ACH is free and US only; wire costs $50 and is the only international option; a rush payout for next-business-day processing also costs $50. There is no check payment.
venues.protection: Not established from the pages read. Fanatics Collect holds the cards in its own vault and handles photographing, listing, payment and ownership transfer, so the seller does not ship to the buyer.
conditions: Weekly Auction listings open at $5. Premier Auction listings open at $1,000, and all lots are unreserved.
An unsold auction lot returns to your vault and is eligible for one more auction. If it fails again it goes back to the vault and cannot be relisted for 90 days.
Weekly Flash listings from the vault must be submitted by 11.59pm PT Wednesday to close that Sunday.

sources.what: The three selling routes, what is accepted, no auction seller fee, the 6% Buy Now fee, the $3 vault fee, opening bids, unsold-lot rules
The 6% and 12% Buy Now tiers, no minimum fee, and the rule for accepted offers. Redirects to support.fanaticscollect.com/en_us/buy-now-fees-ry33QCXaxe
The 20% buyer's premium on both auctions, FanCash No Fees, and the link to the Commission Overview chart. Redirects to support.fanaticscollect.com.
The Commission Overview chart itself, embedded on the How It Works page: the eight hammer bands, the bonus percentages, and the minimum $3 Weekly Auction commission
Confirms Fanatics retired the PWCC brand on 15 July 2024 and that all PWCC services, including the vault, auctions and marketplace, are now Fanatics Collect
Wednesday payout schedule, Tuesday midnight ET deadline, free ACH, $50 wire, $50 rush, no cheques

venues.note: TWO OF ITS OWN PAGES DISAGREE ON THE PREMIER AUCTION MINIMUM. 'Selling on Fanatics Collect' says collectibles sold through the Premier Auction must have an estimated market value of at least $15,000, with lower values needing staff approval. 'How Fanatics Collect works' says the Premier Auction is reserved for collectibles with a market value of at least $10,000. Both were read on the same day. Neither number is treated as settled here. PWCC is not a separate venue any more: pwccmarketplace.com is Fanatics Collect.

venues.name: Troll and Toad
venues.format: You look up your cards on their buylist, submit the list, ship the cards, and they buy them outright at a published price
venues.bestFor: Bulk and mid-range singles. There is no commission and no waiting for a buyer, because there is no buyer: the shop is buying.
venues.access: An account. The buylist cart cannot be checked out without signing in.

fees.note: A buylist has no commission. The price they publish IS the price, and it is well below market because they are reselling. That gap is the cost.

fees.appliesTo: Choosing trade credit instead of money

fees.appliesTo: Their Pokemon Bulk buylist category as published

venues.access: You must be at least 18. An account earns Premier Program points but the buy list itself is a submission, not a listing.

fees.note: Their own wording: 'There are no fees. If an item is not accepted and is returned, there is no cost for return shipping.' As with any buylist, the cost is the buy price, not a fee line.

Collections they travel to collect
fees.note: Their own wording: 'We pay 95% of our buy prices if we come and pick it up to cover our expenses.' The 5% is the cost of not shipping it yourself.

fees.note: Return shipping on anything they decline is free. Packages must arrive within 7 business days of the submission being accepted, and nothing over 50 pounds.

fees.note: Limit one gift code per day per customer.

venues.name: Sportlots
venues.format: A fixed-price seller store, or a '1, 2, 3, SOLD' auction that ends once a lot goes three days without a higher bid
venues.bestFor: Cheap singles in volume. The commission structure is upside down compared with everywhere else and that is the whole point of it.
venues.access: An account with a payment method set up. No subscription fee anywhere in their seller guide.

fees.what: Fixed-price commission, by TOTAL MONTHLY SALES
fees.appliesTo: The seller's total sales for the month, not the individual sale
fees.note: THE RATE IS SET BY YOUR MONTH, NOT BY THE CARD. Sell $4 in a month and they take 75% of it. Sell $1,500 and they take 15%. Nothing else in this file works this way.

fees.what: How expensive cards are counted into that table
fees.rate: Only 50% of the portion of a sale price between $5 and $15 counts, and only 25% of the portion above $15
fees.appliesTo: The figure fed into the monthly fee schedule
fees.note: Their own worked example: a $50 card contributes only $18.75 to the fee schedule, leaving $31.25 of that sale with no fee applied at all. So the headline percentages overstate the take on anything expensive.
Their own wording: 'If no cards sell, there will be no charges.'

fees.appliesTo: Each auction listing, charged when you list
fees.note: Sunk whether or not the lot draws a bid. Optional extras: highlighting $0.10, category-level featured $1.00, site-level featured $2.50, all charged the same way.

fees.appliesTo: PayPal and credit card transaction fees on buyer payments
fees.note: The flat portion is spread across every seller involved in a combined transaction. This is the on-top fee that the commission table does not show.

fees.rate: Seller keeps 100% of the postage charged
fees.appliesTo: Shipping you bill the buyer
fees.note: Sellers set their own postage rates, and set them to $999.99 to opt out.

fees.appliesTo: An optional rebate the seller offers buyers
fees.note: Entirely optional and set by the seller.

venues.payout: PayPal sellers are paid automatically on the 1st of each month to the registered email address. Credit sellers have earnings added to their Sportlots credit balance, and credit withdrawals are processed by hand and can take up to 7 days. Orders must be filled within 5 days of being paid for.
venues.protection: Not established from the pages read.

venues.name: Goldin
venues.format: Weekly Auction and Elite Auction. The fixed-price Marketplace closed on 20 May 2024.
venues.bestFor: Graded and authenticated cards and sealed product. The Weekly Auction takes items valued at $100 or greater; the Elite Auction targets $7,500 and up.
venues.access: Submit through goldin.co/sell for the Weekly Auction, or through a Consignment Director for Elite. Items must be graded or authenticated by an approved company (PSA, Beckett, SGC, CGC certified) with an exception for ungraded factory-encapsulated cards.

fees.what: Seller fee on a lot that sells for $50 hammer or more
fees.rate: No listing fee, 'unless otherwise agreed by the seller and Goldin'
fees.appliesTo: Weekly Auction lots
fees.note: A percentage seller's commission is NOT published anywhere on Goldin's own FAQ. Goldin's visible income on these lots is the 22% buyer's premium. No commission figure is recorded here because none was found on Goldin's own pages, and it may be negotiated per consignment.

fees.what: Seller fee on a lot that sells under $50, or draws no bid
fees.appliesTo: Per lot
fees.note: Weekly lots all start at $10 with no reserve, so a lot that goes cheap still costs you $5. This is a floor that bites downward rather than a percentage.

fees.appliesTo: All memorabilia, sealed boxes, unopened wax boxes and sets
fees.note: Excludes encapsulated or graded items. Authentication, matting and framing may be charged separately, INCLUDING IF AUTHENTICATION FAILS. These are deducted from sale proceeds.

fees.appliesTo: Paid by the buyer
fees.note: Not a seller cost, but it is the money the bidder spends that does not reach you.

fees.appliesTo: Payouts taken by wire

venues.payout: Within 10 business days after Goldin has received both full cleared payment from the buyer AND valid payment instructions from you plus your SSN, ITIN, EIN or self-exempt form. Missing tax information holds the payout.
venues.protection: All sales are final. If a lot draws no bids Goldin may at its discretion relist it in a later auction or return it AT YOUR COST. If an item fails authentication it may be returned at your sole expense, and any authentication, shipping or insurance charges must be paid before it is sent back. Once an item is under contract and up for auction it will not be withdrawn.

sources.what: Auction formats and value thresholds, approved graders, the $5 small-lot fee, the $25 processing fee, the 22% buyer's premium, the 10-business-day payout rule, wire fees, no-reserve $10 opening bids

venues.name: Local card shop
venues.format: Walk in with the cards, walk out with money or store credit the same day
venues.bestFor: Anything, and the only realistic option for bulk that is not worth listing. Also the fastest route for a collection you want gone rather than optimised.
venues.access: None. No account, no application, no subscription, no listing, no photographs.

fees.what: Commission, payment processing, listing, shipping, payout fee
fees.note: There is no third party in the transaction, so there is nothing to take a percentage.

fees.what: The actual cost: the buy price
fees.appliesTo: Every card
fees.note: A SHOP BUYS BELOW MARKET BECAUSE IT HAS TO RESELL AT MARKET. The gap between what it pays you and what it lists the card for is its entire margin, and it also covers the cards that sit unsold. That gap is the fee, it is usually larger than any marketplace commission, and it is the honest trade for cash today with no shipping and no waiting. No Rochester-area shop publishes a buy percentage, so no percentage is recorded here. Ask, and ask more than one.

fees.rate: Commonly offered above the cash price
fees.appliesTo: Sellers willing to take credit rather than money
fees.note: The uplift is set per shop and is not published, so no figure is recorded. Credit is only worth more than cash if you were going to spend it there anyway.

venues.protection: Not applicable in the usual sense: the sale completes in person, so there is no shipping, no buyer dispute window, no chargeback and no payout hold.

venues.name: Card show
venues.type: In person, outright sale or your own table
venues.format: Two different things under one name: sell across the table to the dealers who set up, or rent a table and sell to the public yourself
venues.bestFor: Selling to dealers works for volume and for anything you want turned into cash in an afternoon. Renting a table suits a large enough inventory to justify a day of standing behind it.
venues.access: Selling to dealers needs nothing but admission. Renting a table means booking with the organiser in advance.

fees.what: Commission on a sale to a dealer
fees.note: Same structure as a shop: no commission, and the dealer's buy price below market is the real cost. Several dealers in one room means several offers on the same card in one afternoon, which is the thing a show has that a shop does not.

fees.rate: Varies by show, and some do not state it
